title: Routine Immunization Recovery After the COVID-19 Pandemic— Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, 2020 – 2023
content:
Background: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted routine immunization services worldwide, leading to declines in childhood vaccination coverage and increased numbers of zero-dose (unimmunized) and under-immunized children. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province, Pakistan, also experienced substantial reductions in vaccination coverage. This study assessed the recovery of childhood immunization services in KP following the COVID-19 pandemic.
Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted using aggregated administrative data from the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) Management Information System from January 2020–December 2023. The years 2020–2021 were defined as the COVID-19 period, while 2022–2023 represented the post-COVID-19 recovery period. Vaccination coverage analysis included the following antigens: Bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG), oral poliovirus vaccine first and third doses (OPV1 and OPV3), pentavalent vaccine first and third doses (Penta1 and Penta3), inactivated poliovirus vaccine first dose (IPV1), and measles-rubella vaccine first and second doses (MR1 and MR2). Coverage was analyzed at provincial, divisional, and district levels and mean coverage was compared with paired t-tests, with statistical significance set at p< 0.05.
Results: Vaccination coverage improved significantly for all key antigens during the post-COVID-19 period in KP. Provincial coverage increased from 86% to 104% for BCG, 90% to 106% for OPV1, 82% to 96% for Penta3, 85% to 100% for IPV1, and 81% to 98% for MR1 (all p< 0.001). MR2 showed improvement to a level < 80%, increasing from 65% to 79% (p< 0.001). Recovery was evident across all seven divisions and most districts of the province, with the greatest improvements observed in Peshawar block, a core poliovirus reservoir. Coverage exceeding 100% for selected antigens likely reflected catch-up vaccination of children who had missed routine immunization doses during the pandemic. Year-wise analysis demonstrated a progressive and sustained recovery in immunization coverage.
Conclusions: Routine immunization services in KP recovered substantially following COVID-19-related disruptions. Continued investment in routine immunization, particularly in underperforming districts, is essential to sustain gains, improve childhood population immunity against vaccine-preventable diseases, and strengthen resilience against future public health emergencies.
